title.narrative: Improved decent work employment opportunities through the development of coherent policies aligned to international standards on labour statistics in Papua New Guinea

description.narrative:
The International Labour Organization (ILO) is supporting the Government of Papua New Guinea (PNG) to strengthen its social protection system. A comprehensive Social Protection Diagnostic Assessment (SPDA) was conducted to inform the ongoing review of PNG’s employment laws and to support the implementation of the National Social Protection Policy (NSPP) 2022–2030. The assessment identifies current gaps and provides recommendations to improve coverage and effectiveness, especially for informal and vulnerable workers. In addition to the SPDA, the ILO organized capacity building on social protection at a workshop in November 2024. These activites were funded by the Government of Japan, through its Building Social Safety Nets in Asia and the Pacific (SSN) initiative. Discussions are ongoing to explore opportunities to enhance the system and ensure that all Papua New Guineans have access to adequate and sustainable social protection.
In addition, the ILO is supporting the implementation of PNG’s first-ever National Employment Policy (NEP), which sets out a framework to promote decent, inclusive, and productive employment. The NEP addresses key challenges such as youth unemployment, informality, gender inequality, and the need for skills development. The NEP inludes an action plan and coordination mechanisms. The ILO prepared a report and a conducted a workshop in November 2024 for the Department of Labour and Industrial Relations (DLIR) to enhance implementation efforts and discuss the alignment of the NEP with the new Medium-Term Development Plan (MTDP IV). This activity was funded by the Government of Japan, through its Building Social Safety Nets in Asia and the Pacific (SSN) initiative.
